This review measured the reviewed node's declared gate (tests/data/test_selene_deck.py) in two scratch trees built from the reviewed commit's own object store (git archive of 395b6a68 into $TMPDIR/arms/base and 51f0b617 into $TMPDIR/arms/head, no git worktree created and the reviewed worktree not written). The node is a pure addition: the declared gate target does not exist at the base revision, so the base arm collected nothing (gate-base.log: 'ERROR: file or directory not found', EXIT=4, zero failing ids) and the head arm is green (gate-head.log: 8 passed, EXIT=0, zero failing ids). The green gate does not exercise the defects this review found: test_eqsle_parses_pf_coils asserts the wrong extent convention (width == 2*dr), and no test checks element extents against the facility description or the tf element start/end points.

findings.line: PfElement.width / height (lines 96-104) and the rectangle writers in build_pf_active and build_pf_passive
findings.text: PF and vessel conductor rectangles are emitted at twice their true extent. The committed properties are width = 2.0*dr and height = 2.0*dz, and both writers set rectangle.width/height the same way. The EQSLE.DATA dR/dZ and Va/Vb columns are full extents (pitches): in the OP1 PF1 (CS1) block the 40 elements sit on 4 radial centres spaced 0.08175 and 10 vertical centres spaced 0.15740, and the facility's own laptop description reports CS1 as w=0.327 (= 4*0.08175), h=1.574 (= 10*0.15740); its vv_0 filament is reported w=0.0414, h=0.2497, equal to the deck columns, not their doubles. So each element should be width=dr, height=dz. As committed every element is drawn at double size and overlaps its neighbours by 50%, so the pf_active and pf_passive geometry is wrong by a factor of two. The committed test encodes the wrong convention: test_eqsle_parses_pf_coils asserts first.width == approx(0.2) for dr=0.1 (2*dr), where the deck extent is 0.1. Evidence: reviews/.../*.json, probe-real, and the facility extract in the geometry-source report (ids_laptop_OP1).

The tf conductor elements are degenerate. build_tf assigns the same r_pts/z_pts array to both start_points and end_points, so every element's start equals its end. Read back at DD 4.1.1 from the real deck, conductor0 and conductor1 each report start_r == end_r and start_z == end_z element-for-element (arrays equal, confirmed by np.array_equal), with types all 1. Per the DD, tf/coil/conductor/elements/start_points and end_points are the two endpoints of each segment, so the emitted TF conductor path is a list of zero-length segments carrying no geometry. Arc segments contribute only their start point (_tf_section_points appends seg.params[0], seg.params[1] for an arc). The test only asserts start_r.size >= 1, so the degeneracy is not caught.

The wall limiter outline drops every arc. _wall_outline appends only segments whose kind == 'line'; the real limiter/first-wall table has 43 segments, 33 line and 10 arc, and the 10 arcs are silently skipped when building wall/description_2d/limiter/unit/outline. The outline is therefore a set of disconnected polylines with the arc spans missing (39 points emitted from 33 line segments), so the emitted first-wall contour is incomplete. The test asserts only outline_r.size >= 2, so the missing arcs are not caught.

tf/coil[:]/turns is written as a guessed 0 and tf/coils_n as a guessed 18. Plan section 4 says the tf IDS is populated from the deck's TF description with tf/coil/turns and tf/b_field_phi_vacuum_r derived from a declared relation. The committed code hard-codes tf_turns = 0 (with a comment that the turn count is not inferred) and writes 18 coils, and it never writes tf/b_field_phi_vacuum_r into the IDS at all: derive_b_field_phi_vacuum_r is placed in the receipt dict under a non-DD key 'tf_b_field_phi_vacuum_r' only when tf_current is passed. The one COCOS-dependent tf field the plan names is thus absent from the IDS.

The reviewed worktree carries 84 uncommitted insertions in imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py (11 hunks, +84/-23) that supersede the reviewed commit and are not landed anywhere: git log --all shows no commit after 51f0b617 touching the file and branch -a --contains 51f0b617 is empty. The uncommitted diff corrects the width/height factor of two described above (width = dr, not 2*dr), replaces the mean resistivity with one loop per contiguous resistivity block, leaves tf turns/coils_n unset with a validation_gaps receipt entry instead of guessed zeros, and documents the full-extent convention. Because these edits are uncommitted they are invisible to the ledger and would be lost if the worktree were reclaimed. The delivered artifact is therefore not the worktree's final state, and the commit's own tests (which assert width == 2*dr) are already red against the on-disk module.

findings.line: build_pf_passive (mean resistivity) and the plan's vessel-resistivity statement
findings.text: pf_passive/loop/resistivity is emitted as the mean of the filaments. The DD carries resistivity only at loop level (pf_passive/loop/resistivity, FLT_0D) with no element leaf, so a per-filament value cannot be carried directly. But the OP1 EQSLE.DATA vessel block is not uniform: of its 120 rows, 63 carry 7.76e-07 and 57 carry 7.20E-007, so the emitted 7.494e-07 is no filament's value and is asserted rather than derived. Plan section 4 states the OP1 vessel as '120 filaments at 7.76e-7 ohm.m', which this review measures to be inaccurate. The plan statement should be corrected and the collapse recorded (the uncommitted revision splits into blocks and records it).

The probe angle is written to magnetics/b_field_pol_probe/poloidal_angle as radians (deg2rad of the geo.in column). This review confirms the geo.in column is in degrees (the 17 rows sweep 0.28 to 350.24), so the conversion itself is correct; the evidence fragment states it plainly. Plan section 4 asks the probe angle to be marked unknown-unvalidated until section 6 settles its sense against vacuum data, and the emitted value carries no such qualification. Minor, but the plan's qualification is not represented in the output.
